drills.q: Generate all subsets of a set of distinct integers.
drills.a: Record every partial path as a valid subset (append a copy); loop from a start index, choose (append), explore (recurse with i+1), unchoose (pop) after the call returns.

drills.q: Generate all permutations of a set of distinct integers.
drills.a: Track a used[] boolean array instead of a start index; choose by marking used and appending, explore recursively when the path reaches full length, unchoose by unmarking and popping.

drills.q: Place N queens on an N x N board so none attack each other; return all valid placements.
drills.a: Track occupied columns and both diagonals (row-col, row+col) in sets; at each row, only recurse into columns with no conflict, checked before the recursive call, then unchoose after it returns.

drills.q: Find all combinations of candidates (each reusable unlimited times) summing to a target.
drills.a: Sort candidates; recurse with the same start index i (not i+1) to allow reuse; prune by breaking the loop once candidates[i] exceeds the remaining target.

drills.q: Partition a string into substrings that are all palindromes; return all such partitions, and describe how to avoid recomputing palindrome checks.
drills.a: Only recurse into a substring if it's already verified to be a palindrome, checked before recursing; precompute a 2D isPalindrome[i][j] table via DP in O(n^2) so each check is O(1) instead of O(n).

drills.q: Determine if an array can be partitioned into k subsets of equal sum, and explain why filling one bucket at a time prunes better than assigning each element to a bucket independently.
drills.a: Compute target=total/k (fail if not divisible), then backtrack filling one subset up to the target sum before moving to the next, abandoning a subset the moment its running sum exceeds target -- this collapses many equivalent element-orderings that element-to-bucket assignment (k^n raw possibilities) would otherwise explore separately.
